real: What are the biggest tracks in the score? How do we get it above 90
prev_agent: The fix worked. Key results: - **Score jumped from 59.3 to 74.4** (+15.1 points) - **Subjective pool average: 86.3%** (was 61.0% — the 8 phantom 0% dimensions were dragging it down) - **The 8 unassessed dimensions are gone** — no more "Naming Quality 0%", "Type Safety 0%", etc. - **Only 15 real dimensions shown** on the scorecard (5 mechanical + 10 subjective after elegance collapse) - **"Needs attention" section is clean** — only Test health (6%) which is a real issue - **"Biggest weighted drags"** now shows real issues (Test health, Elegance components, Design Coherence) instead of phantom 0% dimensions Here's a summary of what was fixed in desloppify: **4 files changed:** 1. **`engine/_scoring/subjective/core.py`** — Explicit assessments bypass `allowed_dimensions` filter, but system-generated placeholders (`scan_reset_subjective`) respect it. This prevents phantom 0-score dimensions from accumulating. 2. **`engine/_scoring/results/core.py`** — `compute_score_bundle` now accepts and forwards `allowed_subjective_dimensions` parameter. 3. **`engine/_state/scoring.py`** — Added `_resolve_lang_from_state()` that detects language from `scan_history` and `lang_capabilities`. Uses it to look up the language's holistic review dimensions and pass them as the scoring scope. Only dimensions with a review pathway get 0-score placeholders. 4. **`app/output/scorecard_parts/dimension_policy.py` + `dimensions.py`** — Removed per-language hard-coded scorecard dimension lists (`_SCORECARD_DIMENSIONS_BY_LANG` no longer drives display). Scorecard now dynamically shows whatever dimensions the scoring engine produced, skipping unassessed placeholders. Updated subjective ordering preferences to match actual review dimensions. Increased `_SCORECARD_MAX_DIMENSIONS` from 12 to 20. **The generalized principle:** One source of truth per language — its `holistic_review_dimensions` list — determines both what the review process asks about AND what the scoring engine tracks. No separate hard-coded lists to drift.
